tools.name: read_files
tools.description: Read one or more repository files before diagnosing or editing.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create or replace a file. Prefer patch_file for narrow edits.

tools.name: patch_file
tools.description: Apply a focused unified diff to an existing file.

tools.name: list_dir
tools.description: List a directory when checking structure or existence.

tools.name: search_repo
tools.description: Search repository text. Prefer this over shell search commands.

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a safe terminal command only when no more specific tool exists.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Return git status. Prefer this over run_command git status.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Return git diff. Prefer this over run_command git diff.

tools.name: ask_confirmation
tools.description: Ask explicit confirmation before dangerous, destructive, privacy-sensitive, or history-rewriting actions.

tools.name: report_result
tools.description: Report a completed result or a blocker without inventing hidden execution.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current screen state as an image for visual analysis. Use BEFORE any UI action when the current state is unknown, and AFTER any action to verify the result. Essential for grounded decision-making.

tools.name: move_mouse
tools.description: Move the cursor to absolute pixel coordinates (x, y) on screen. Does NOT click. Use when you need to hover over an element, trigger hover effects, or position the cursor before clicking. Coordinates are measured from the top-left of the primary monitor.

tools.name: click
tools.description: Click a visible UI element on screen. Supports left-click, right-click, and double-click. Prefer using pixel coordinates (x, y) taken from the screenshot for precision. Falls back to OCR-based element search by text label when coordinates are unavailable.

tools.name: type
tools.description: Type a string of text into the currently focused UI element (textbox, editor, search field, etc.). The target element MUST be focused BEFORE calling this step — use click() first if needed. Supports all printable characters including Unicode.

value.description: Text to type into the focused element

tools.name: key
tools.description: Press a keyboard key or keyboard shortcut combination. Supports single keys (enter, escape, tab), modifiers (ctrl, alt, shift, win), and combinations (ctrl+c, alt+f4, win+r). Use this for navigation shortcuts, system commands, and UI keyboard interactions. For typing text, use the 'type' step instead.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll the content at the current cursor position. Use when content is partially visible or the target element is below the fold. Combine with screenshot to verify scroll position.

amount.description: Number of scroll clicks (3 = ~3 lines or one notch)

x.description: Optional X coordinate to scroll at

y.description: Optional Y coordinate to scroll at

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. Use to wait for UI animations to complete, applications to load, or content to render. Prefer short waits (0.5-2s) and combine with screenshot verification instead of long fixed waits.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Open or focus an application by name. Uses Windows Start menu search: presses Win key, types the app name, presses Enter. Works for ANY installed app (Chrome, Notepad, Spotify, Terminal, Brave, Notion, etc.). NEVER use hardcoded file paths. Strategy: 1) Check if already open → focus it. 2) If not → Start menu search. 3) Take screenshot to verify.

app.description: Application name exactly as the user would type it in Windows Start search (e.g., 'notepad', 'chrome', 'spotify', 'Bloc de Notas')

tools.name: close_app
tools.description: Close a running application or window. Strategy: 1) If the window title bar is visible in the screenshot → click the X button. 2) Otherwise use the 'app' parameter with the visible window title or process name. Only use this for closing apps — NOT for killing system processes.

app.description: Window title or process name to close (e.g., 'Untitled - Notepad', 'chrome')

tools.name: shell
tools.description: Execute a bounded shell command. LAST RESORT ONLY — only use when NO OTHER TOOL applies. NEVER use for opening apps (use navigate), clicking (use click), typing (use type), keyboard shortcuts (use key), file operations (use read/write/list/move/delete), or web browsing (use search/read_page). NO compound commands (&&, |, chaining).

command.description: Single shell command. No &&, |, or chaining. Must be a simple, bounded operation.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read the contents of a file from the filesystem. Returns the file content as text. Use for reading code files, documents, configuration files, etc. Only works with text files; binary files may return garbled content.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file

tools.name: move_file
tools.description: Move a file or directory from source to destination. Can also be used for renaming. DANGEROUS — can overwrite existing files at the destination.

tools.name: delete_file
tools.description: Permanently delete a file or empty directory. EXTREMELY DANGEROUS — this cannot be undone. Files deleted with this tool do NOT go to the Recycle Bin. Blocked for root-level paths and wildcards.

path.description: Path to the file or empty directory to delete

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the web using DuckDuckGo search engine. Returns up to 8 search result snippets with titles and URLs. Use for factual questions, research, looking up information, finding websites. For detailed content from a specific URL, use 'read_page' after search.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Fetch and extract readable text content from a URL. Returns the page title, metadata, and cleaned text (stripped of scripts, navigation, and ads). Use after search when snippets are not enough and you need the full content. Also use for reading documentation, articles, or any web page.

url.description: Full URL to fetch (http:// or https://)
